images.title: Sorting numbers by factors
images.purpose: Recap the sort: primes, composites (including odd ones) and 1 on its own.
images.composition: Three labelled trays in a row across the frame, each holding a few number cards, with white space between trays.
exact_structure: Left tray outlined green (#009E73), headed Prime, holds exactly 2 cards: 2 and 13.
Middle tray outlined vermilion (#D55E00), headed Composite, holds exactly 2 cards: 9 with 3 × 3 written small under it, and 15 with 3 × 5 written small under it.
Right tray outlined grey (#6B7280), smaller, headed Neither, holds exactly 1 card: 1.
All cards are plain white with dark outlines; no other cards.
rejection: any number in the wrong tray, or 1 placed with the primes
any extra card beyond the 5 listed
a wrong factor pair under 9 or 15
images.takeaway: Check the factors, not whether a number is odd: 9 and 15 are odd but composite, and 1 is neither.
images.description: Three trays labelled Prime, Composite and Neither holding 2 and 13, then 9 and 15 with their factors, then 1.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Stress that odd numbers can be composite; find a factor pair before deciding.

image_decisions.why: A compact sorting recap prepares students for the prime or composite practice.
